scenes.title: A digital twin must carry the right state
scenes.detail: A useful Gaussian twin must reproduce the physical robot state that generated each observation, not only its visual appearance.
scenes.caption: KineSync-GS addresses a missing link in Real2Sim2Real. Gaussian Splatting can reproduce a robot visually, but a useful digital twin must also represent the physical robot's articulated state at the correct time.

scenes.title: Image fitting and state recovery can diverge
scenes.detail: A delayed or conflicting image can reward a pose that renders better while moving the articulated state farther from the physical robot.
scenes.caption: The difficulty appears when cameras are delayed or views disagree. Direct inverse rendering can keep lowering image error while joint error rises. A visually improved estimate therefore cannot receive automatic authority to modify the twin.

scenes.title: Separate estimation from state-changing authority
scenes.detail: Rendering or motion proposes a bounded correction. Separate evidence decides whether that proposal becomes the published state.
scenes.caption: KineSync-GS separates two decisions. Rendering or motion first proposes a bounded correction. Cross-view or motion evidence then determines whether the proposal is committed as a verified update or the incoming measurement is preserved.

scenes.title: Cross-view evidence verifies one coordinated state
scenes.detail: Kinematics binds Gaussians to links, multi-view fitting proposes one joint vector, and view-specific estimates verify the complete correction.
scenes.formula: q+ = qᵐ + SI b tanh(z),   esp = (r, g, a, d)
scenes.caption: For spatial synchronization, fixed kinematics bind Gaussians to robot links and inverse rendering estimates one coordinated joint correction. View-specific estimates provide evidence for the complete proposal, which is committed atomically or rejected as a whole.

scenes.title: Motion evidence aligns cameras with telemetry
scenes.detail: Cross-modal motion proposes residual lag after native-delay correction, then timing evidence verifies whether the state stream should be resampled.
scenes.formula: Δt+ = arg maxτ corr(vimage(t), vjoint(t + τ))
scenes.caption: The temporal path instantiates the same contract. Image and telemetry motion propose a residual lag after native-delay correction. Timing evidence then selects corrected resampling or preserves the original camera-to-state association.

scenes.title: Whole-state verification resolves view conflict
scenes.detail: The verifier retains every useful coordinated proposal while rejecting updates that would move the twin away from the physical state.
scenes.caption: On twelve held-out Franka poses and forty-eight view-offset conditions, KineSync-GS reduces whole-state joint error from zero point five nine zero to zero point three two two degrees. It retains all twelve helpful proposals and makes no harmful update.

scenes.title: Factorized evidence sharpens update decisions
scenes.detail: Persistent camera and joint calibration are factorized before evaluation; component re-verification then preserves successful proposals.
scenes.formula: shared joint zero + view-specific camera residual
scenes.caption: The mechanism ablations explain this selectivity. Factorized calibration raises dual-view recovery from forty-two point eight six to eighty point nine five percent, while component re-verification retains eighty-eight point eight nine percent of successful proposals.

scenes.title: The state contract transfers to physical PiPER motion
scenes.detail: Matched physical views supply cross-view evidence while the Gaussian backend publishes one task-ready articulated state stream.
scenes.formula: camera views → proposal → cross-view evidence → qˢ(t)
scenes.caption: Real-world PiPER recordings evaluate the same interface under physical motion and matched head and wrist cameras. Cross-view evidence aligns the rendered gripper while the verified state remains available throughout corn-to-plate execution.

scenes.title: Spatial and temporal evidence work together online
scenes.detail: The online chain associates asynchronous measurements, verifies spatial recovery, and publishes a synchronized state for every task.
scenes.formula: camera + telemetry → temporal verify → spatial verify → qˢ
scenes.caption: In the complete online chain, spatial and temporal evidence are complementary. KineSync-GS reaches three point zero seven milliradians qMAE with eighty-three point zero five percent recovery and only zero point three six percent harmful updates.

scenes.title: A synchronized state improves an unchanged policy
scenes.detail: Raw and synchronized states feed the same policy under the same task budget, isolating the effect of state synchronization.
scenes.formula: π(a | qraw)  versus  π(a | qˢ),   π fixed
scenes.caption: Most importantly, synchronization improves downstream manipulation without changing the policy. Across two hundred forty paired real-robot episodes, task-macro success rises from fifty-eight point three three to seventy-one point six seven percent.

scenes.title: One verified state interface across robot stacks
scenes.detail: Robot-specific renderers and camera layouts remain behind adapters while simulators and policies consume one synchronized state contract.
scenes.formula: robot adapters → KineSync-GS state bus → twin / simulator / policy
scenes.caption: KineSync-GS turns visual evidence into a verified state-changing interface across Gaussian twins, simulators, and downstream robot policies.
